checks.name: A4-validation-and-the-partial-object-refusal-through-the-transport
checks.summary: PASS: 4 accepted literals and 22 refused literals driven as real HTTP requests with a runner session. Accepted with 200 and a reported row: [0.1.0, 64-hex, 1, 1]; [0.1.0-dev, ..., 2, 7]; [1.0.0-rc.1, ..., 3, 9]; [10.20.30, ..., 1, 4096]. Refused with 400: version 1.2 (bare major.minor), v1.2.3 (leading v), 1.2.3-RC1 (uppercase prerelease), "" (empty string), 1.2.3.4, 1.2.3- ; digest at 63 characters, at 65 characters, uppercase, non-hex; schema_min 0, schema_max below schema_min, schema_max 4097 above the ceiling, schema_min 4097 above the ceiling; and eight partial objects -- schema_max with no schema_min, schema_min alone, version alone, digest alone, interval with no binary, binary with no interval, everything but schema_min, and the wholly empty object {}. PARTIAL-OBJECT VERDICT AT THE TRANSPORT: every one of those 22 requests returned HTTP 400 and, on the subsequent GET /v1/runners, the runners array was EMPTY and intersection_state was unknown -- so the refused heartbeat stored no report and left no trace at all, and in particular schema_max without schema_min was never stored as an interval starting at zero. Omitting runner_version entirely returned HTTP 200 with the Runner enumerating as report_state not-reported, with the keys version, binary_sha256, schema_min, schema_max and reported_at all absent from the row, and intersection_state unknown. An unknown field inside runner_version (contract_release) returned 400, from DisallowUnknownFields at internal/api/api.go:830 plus additionalProperties:false in the contract. A Runner-supplied reported_at inside runner_version also returned 400, for the same reason: the field does not exist on the request object. Every pre-existing heartbeat assertion still passes unchanged.

checks.name: A10-api-surface
checks.summary: PASS. GET /v1/runners returns 401 unauthenticated, 403 for the runner role and 200 for the owner; POST to the same path returns 405, because there is deliberately no reporting endpoint there. The response document's top-level keys are exactly runners, runner_count, truncated, intersection_state and, when the state is non-empty, intersection_schema_min and intersection_schema_max; a runner row's keys are exactly runner_id, report_state and, when a report was read, version, binary_sha256, schema_min, schema_max, reported_at. Any other key fails the test. The raw response body is also searched for contract_release, contract_digest, runner_api, bundle_digest, candidate_id, key_id, algorithm, TODO, placeholder, unknown-version and 0.0.0, and contains none of them, so there is no synthetic or placeholder value. contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml gained the /v1/runners path (operationId listRunners, security iapOwner) and three schemas: RunnerVersionReport with additionalProperties:false and required [version, binary_sha256, schema_min, schema_max] -- every field of the request object is required, which is what makes a partial object a contract violation as well as a 400 -- plus RunnerVersionRow and RunnerListResponse, both additionalProperties:false. HeartbeatRequest gained runner_version as a $ref and keeps additionalProperties:false. On the two response schemas, required lists only the always-present fields (runner_id and report_state; runners, runner_count, truncated, intersection_state) because a coordinate that was never reported must be absent rather than present-and-empty -- that is the same acceptance item A6(a). The document parses as YAML with 23 paths. Every existing openapi-conformance assertion still passes: internal/contracts is green (including openAPIDeclaredPaths in release_contract_test.go) and so is internal/release.

checks.name: A8-firestore-read-count-does-not-vary-with-requirement-count
checks.summary: PASS against the local Firestore emulator. The trued-up quota total is the adapter's own record of the documents a transaction actually read (trueUpQuota accounts actual reads as len(u.cache)), so the delta across one GET /v1/runners is the measured read count. Measured against a fixture exactly at the enumeration bound -- 32 Runners, every one known and every one reporting: 65 reads with 3 Requirements in the store and 65 reads with 11 Requirements in the store. The two figures are equal, so the read count does not vary with the Requirement count, and both are exactly the declared bound 2*MaxRunnerVersionReports+1 = 65: two per-machine collections (runner_observations and runner_version_reports) plus the quota document. Writes for the same read: exactly 1 in both measurements, the per-transaction quota reservation every bounded owner read already writes -- so one GET /v1/runners writes no application record and enqueues no outbox item.

checks.name: A9-the-same-behavioural-table-against-the-firestore-adapter
checks.summary: Both PASS against the local Firestore emulator. TestRunnerVersionReportBehaviouralTableOnFirestore: the Firestore adapter satisfied the same 5 shared cases from application.RunnerVersionReportCases() that internal/store/memory runs, so the memory store cannot pass behaviour this adapter does not implement. Last-writer-wins per RunnerID, a Runner known only through a report-less heartbeat enumerating with zero coordinates, RunnerID-ascending order, and truncation at the bound are all asserted here too, and every read happens in a transaction separate from every write. TestRunnerVersionReportRollbackLeaksNothingOnFirestore: a rolled-back Firestore transaction commits no report -- neither the keyed read nor the enumeration sees it -- and a report with an empty runner id is refused. The new collection runner_version_reports needs no composite index: RunnerVersionReports reads two bounded collections with no ordering and no predicate, exactly as Repositories does, so firestore.indexes.json is untouched. No existing operation's quota reservation shape changed. Emulator success is evidence about this adapter's transaction wiring, never about real Firestore contention, IAM or billing.

checks.name: A13-owner-console
checks.summary: PASS. One self-contained block was appended to internal/web/owner.html and one to internal/web/owner.js, each introduced by a comment naming V2-069, at the end of the file, changing no existing byte -- verified independently of the test by a byte-offset comparison against a copy of each file taken before the edit: owner.html differs first at offset 5020 of 5094, the insertion is 1583 bytes and the remaining suffix is identical, and the whole of owner.js's previous 10750 bytes is a byte-identical prefix of the new file (cmp). The html block is the last section of <main>, which is the tail of the rendered page because an HTML document has no valid tail after </html>. The rendered console carries runners-title, runners-refresh, runners-count, runners-silent, runners-intersection, runners-intersection-reason and runners-rows, and still carries every pre-existing surface including the three sibling tasks' sections (capture, control, queue, repository, repository-list, Release evidence, release-conditions, backlog-rows). A reader sees which Runners have not reported without parsing anything: the block renders a dedicated named list, 'Machines that have not reported a version', with one row per Runner reading either 'has never reported a version' or 'reported once, then went quiet', and a separate 'shared interval' line that reads 'shared interval: unknown' with the reason 'At least one machine has not reported a version, so the shared interval cannot be stated.' The block contains no JSON.stringify, so it renders named rows rather than raw JSON, and the assertion is scoped to the V2-069 block so the pre-existing queue block's own raw-JSON rendering cannot satisfy it. The block references no http:// or https:// URL, no CDN, no importScripts, no setInterval, no setTimeout and no @font-face: internal/web is embedded and stays self-contained, and the block starts no timer and no poll loop. The rendered markup contains no credential-shaped value (password, secret, api_key, apikey, 'bearer ', authorization:, private_key) and no email-shaped value: it contains no at-sign at all, which is the strictest form of that check. The console does not claim a measurement it lacks: 'every machine reported', 'versions are compatible' and 'capability exercised' are all absent.

checks.name: canonical-schema-counter-has-no-owner
checks.summary: Six matching lines, and every one is a parameter or a use of that parameter: the signatures of Verify at internal/update/update.go:127, Install at :220 and VerifyInstalled at :296, and the comparisons at :165 and :221 and :301. No constant, field, record or store anywhere in the repository owns a canonical schema value. Consequence, stated as a fact and not as a limitation to be worked around: the intersection this task computes CAN be reported but GATES NOTHING, because there is nothing to compare it against and no operation whose refusal would consume it. This task therefore introduces no canonical schema counter and no advance operation, and neither this record, the API response, the owner console nor docs/operations/runner-version-report.md claims that the intersection gates, permits or refuses anything. The refusal that consumes it belongs to whoever owns the advance (V2-070's four-stage migration); that split is recorded here with a named owner rather than closed by invention. The Work Order's :41 and :71 line numbers for currentSchema are stale.
